title: Intrinsically Stretchable Fully π‐Conjugated Polymer Films Enabled by Supramolecular Plasticized Micro‐Crosslinking‐Network for Flexible Polymer Light‐Emitting Diodes
authors: Dunliang He; Jiabin Liu; Zhiyang Sun; Shuang Li; Tingting Yang; Haixu Zhao; Rui Gao; Zhiqiang Zhuo; Mingjian Ni; Wenyu Chen; Lili Sun; Xiang An; Ning Sun; Jingyao Ma; Man Xu; Yu Cheng; Jianming Zhang; Wei Huang; Jinyi Lin
abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable fully π‐conjugated polymers (FπCPs) films with a fantastic optoelectronic property and outstanding deformation tolerance capacity, is a promising candidate for the fabrication of flexible optoelectronics devices. However, previous reported stretchable FπCPs films undergo irreversible chain slippage and alignment upon strain release, leading to plastic deformation, and consequently severe performance degradation during cyclic‐deformation operation. Herein, we proposed a supramolecular soft‐micro‐crosslinked strategy to achieve the stretchable p ‐ n FπCPs (P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI) films with a recoverable‐deformation ability for the flexible electronics. Three‐dimensional (3D) supramolecular micro‐crosslinked network formed by oxime‐urethane and hydrogen bonds allow for the excellent elastic deformation to dissipate transient stress while fundamentally suppressing permanent chain slippage. Micro‐crosslinked p ‐ n FπCPs free‐standing films achieved an elongation at break of > 40%. Flexible PLED based on P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI showed a stable green emission with brightness of ∼3300 cd cm −2 . Meanwhile, the performance of transferred PLED based on stretchable micro‐crosslinked films are independent on the tensile ratio (>20%) with a maximum brightness of ∼2000 cd m −2 , revealed the excellent cycle‐deformation‐stability than device based on crosslinked films. Therefore, these supramolecular micro‐crosslinked networks can enhance instantaneous toughness and confer a critical resistance to long‐term stress relaxation and plastic deformation, further ensure the device excellent deformation stability.

title: Rational Selection of Hole Contacts with an Organic Light-Emitting Diode Industry p-Dopant for Fully Vacuum-Processed Perovskite/Silicon Tandems
authors: Su Ji Moon; Sumin Ji; Minjun Cho; Seung-Woo Kim; Moonhoe Kim; Jino Im; JungYup Yang; Nam Joong Jeon; Beom-Soo Kim
abstract: Abstract Translating perovskite/silicon tandems to fully vacuum-based manufacturing requires vacuum-compatible p-doped hole contacts, yet clear selection criteria for doped hole-transport materials (HTMs) remain underdeveloped compared with C60-based electron contacts. Here, we report a fully vacuum-processed perovskite/silicon tandem reaching 29.1% power conversion efficiency, among the highest reported for tandems with fully vacuum-deposited perovskite top cells, enabled by transferring the organic light-emitting diode (OLED)-industry p-dopant NDP-9 and an evaporable arylamine HTM into the perovskite stack. Comparing TaTm, Spiro-TTB, and TAPC shows that contact selection does not follow apparent host–dopant interaction strength derived from theoretical calculations or conventional optical, vibrational, and photoemission spectroscopies. Instead, device-level charge extraction and recombination metrics identify NDP-9-doped TaTm as the most effective contact, also yielding 20.0% in a single-junction 1.70 eV wide-bandgap cell. These results point to transport-based screening as a practical route to selecting vacuum-compatible doped hole contacts.

title: Precision Synthesis of Living Anionic Polymer Crosslinked Nanorods in Concentrated Solutions
Optimizing Re-Crosslinkable Preformed Particle Gel Injection Parameters Under Reservoir Uncertainty in Strongly Heterogeneous Carbonate Reservoirs
authors: Hualei Xu; Wei Kuang; Wenqi Zhang; Cheng Cai; Houshun Jiang; Jie Wang
abstract: Preferential water channeling in strongly heterogeneous carbonate reservoirs causes ineffective water circulation and uneven interlayer sweep, limiting remaining-oil recovery and complicating re-crosslinkable preformed particle gel (RPPG) treatment design. A representative CMG-STARS sector model, informed by field-derived properties and the reported Mishrif Formation architecture at Halfaya, coupled size-dependent RPPG transport, retention, swelling, staged re-crosslinking, and permeability reduction with flow redistribution. Single-factor and orthogonal simulations established injection-parameter ranges. Response-surface modeling, Morris screening, and Sobol variance decomposition quantified sensitivities and interactions among eight formulation and treatment inputs. Injection concentration, rate, timing, and volume were jointly optimized using designed exploration and controlled evolution (DECE) in CMOST, followed by full-physics verification. With optimized injection settings fixed, uncertainty in 18 reservoir and RPPG-retention parameters was propagated using surrogate-assisted Monte Carlo analysis. Results showed the following. (1) All four injection parameters affected recovery factor nonlinearly. Injection volume and timing dominated, with Sobol total-effect indices of 46.1% and 32.6%, respectively. Interactions accounted for approximately 64% of the total effect of injection volume. (2) DECE optimization achieved a final recovery factor of 43.8%, exceeding the orthogonally selected scheme and baseline waterflooding by 1.6 and approximately 6.1 percentage points, respectively. (3) Under the prescribed uncertainty distributions, the probabilities of the final recovery factor equaling or exceeding 40.30%, 43.43%, and 45.58% were 90%, 50%, and 10%, respectively. The deterministic result (43.8%) was close to the median (43.43%) and lay within the main uncertainty-response range, supporting robustness under the assessed conditions. The integrated workflow supports quantitative RPPG treatment design and performance assessment under reservoir uncertainty.

title: A Novel Sensitive and Stretchable TPU/MXene Film-Based Strain Sensor
authors: Anbang Chen; Chong Wang; Wentao Jiang
abstract: The emergence of embodiment intelligence raises an immediate demand for high-performance strain sensors with adjustable large working ranges to enable precise deformation measurements. Herein, a high-performance strain sensor based on TPU/MXene composite films is fabricated via an ultrasonic anchoring strategy, and its sensing mechanism is investigated based on the piezoresistive effect. Benefiting from the synergistic sensing effect of the embedded conductive network constructed by ultrasonic anchoring and the reversible sliding behavior of surface conductive units, the proposed sensor successfully overcomes the narrow strain range limitation of conventional MXene-based strain sensors. The resulting TPU/MXene sensor delivers an ultra-wide sensing range of 0-330 % with a maximum gauge factor of 196.4. In the low-strain region (0-100 %), it exhibits reliable linearity (R² ≈ 0.99), and its signal output remains stable after 1000 tensile cycles. Besides, the optimized TPU/MXene sensor is demonstrated for bending‑deformation measurement on a silicone rod under different cyclic bending angles. This work provides a feasible preparation strategy for high-stretchability and high-sensitivity MXene-based flexible strain sensors, and shows great application potential in flexible deformation monitoring.
